title: Litres and cubic metres
hook: A thousand litres is not a thousand cubic metres.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert a meter quantity from litres to cubic metres.

misconception: A number can keep the same digits when its volume unit changes.
objective: Convert a meter quantity from litres to cubic metres.

claims.text: A converts litres to cubic metres by dividing by 1,000. B incorrectly keeps the same numeric digits. Scaled model; unit model; 1000L=1m³; B deliberately wrong.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Litres=1500L, A=1.5m³ and B=1,500m³. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",1000]; B="x"; x denotes Litres. At x=1500, A=1.5, B=1500; recall at x=1800: B=1800. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: Changing units can require changing the number. One cubic metre contains one thousand litres, so dividing by one thousand preserves the volume. Keeping the digits while changing the unit describes a different volume.
